record.field: The person who enquired. On this pivot it is one row per enquiry, so the same person can appear twice if they came back in a later month.
The patient record this enquiry was matched to. Empty means the enquiry was never linked to a client — usually because it never became a booking.
Whatever address arrived with the enquiry. Often blank on Zalo and hotline arrivals, which is normal, not missing data.
Who owns this enquiry. Not who replied to it — ownership and the last reply can be two different people.
Where this enquiry reached in the lifecycle: New, Lead, Appointment Scheduled, Service Used, or the Cancelled / Spam branch. It is what the Dashboard counts.

The date of the next scheduled follow-up on this contact — the one the Activities board manages. Blank means nothing is scheduled, which on a Lead is the thing to notice: it is how a lead goes quiet without anyone deciding to drop it. Red means overdue.
The person as they identified themselves. In home care this is often a son or daughter rather than the patient.
The lifecycle state this record is in. Moving it forward should record something that really happened; it is not a way to tidy the list.
Where this enquiry arrived from. It is the channel it came in on, which is not always what produced it — a website advert can produce a Zalo message.
The number to reach them on, and the identifier the duplicate check matches against. Match on this, never on the name.
Who is responsible for this contact today. Reassigning it is how work moves at handover.
A triage number computed from status, waiting time and watch phrases. It is a queue position, never a clinical severity — a 110 means look now, not that the patient is critical.
Needs reply, Waiting or Closed — plus Junk? as a branch off to the side. Sending a reply moves it to Waiting automatically.
Which channel the latest message arrived on. One conversation can span several — the row merges them.
Who claimed this conversation. Unclaimed means anyone can take it; claimed means everyone else should leave it alone.
A phrase on the clinic's watch list appeared in an inbound message. It raises the queue position; it says nothing about what is wrong with the patient.
The window every figure on this screen is filtered to — cards, charts and feeds alike. Read no number here without checking it.
How many enquiries arrived today. A day figure — it never describes the same window as Conversion Rate.
Promises made and not yet kept. Compare it with your team's capacity, not with zero — it is the earliest sign someone will be forgotten.
Bookings divided by REAL enquiries — spam is excluded from the denominator on purpose, so that a month with more junk cannot look better.
Spam as a share of everything that arrived. A low rate is not automatically good news: it can simply mean nobody is marking spam, which quietly inflates every other number.
To-Do, Call, Meeting, Email or Document. The type decides nothing on its own — it is there so a shift can scan for the work it can actually do now.
When this was promised for. Filtering to Today hides everything that was due yesterday and never happened — which is the work most likely to become a complaint.
Who will do it. Assigning everything to yourself makes it invisible as team work, and it simply does not happen if you are off sick.
The person this promise was made to. An activity cannot exist on its own — it always hangs off a contact.
Where this channel is in its connection lifecycle. It is derived from the readiness checks and audited — never typed in by hand.
Which account this connection actually points at — the Zalo OA, the Facebook page. This is where a catchment area comes from for channel traffic.
What has been proven about this connection. They show it is capable; only real traffic shows it works.
Exactly what the channel sent, unedited. These records cannot be changed — that is what lets you tell 'no number was given' apart from 'someone removed it'.
Available only when there is something to reach the person by — a contact, a phone number or an email. Greyed out means the arrival carries none, so converting would create a contact nobody can call.
Records a judgement — 'this was not a patient' — against your name. It is the right action when that is true, and not a way to clear the badge count.
Which advert or link produced this arrival. Blank means the tag never reached us, and those land in Unmatched campaigns.
Where the click came from and how — google/cpc, facebook/social. It describes the click, not the person.
The page they actually read. Useful when a campaign brings volume but the page it points at does not ask for a phone number.
How many arrivals this campaign produced. It is a volume, not an outcome — whether they became bookings is on Lead Analysis.
